source_policy.allowed_sources: Current official college catalog program, option-menu, and policy pages only.
source_policy.schedule_rule: A semester grid is excluded when a separate requirements list exists. Blue Ridge's grid is retained and reorganized because the current catalog publishes it as the only course-requirement structure; semester placement itself is not a requirement.
source_policy.advisory_exclusion: Recommendations, transfer-destination advice, and prospective course-availability notes are recorded as context but are not promoted to AND requirements.
source_policy.arithmetic_rule: Published credit contradictions remain visible. No unprinted filler course or compensating-credit rule is invented to force a path to close.

findings: Blue Ridge publishes a current Associate of Science degree with a Computer Science major and a 60-62 credit total.
Brightpoint publishes a current Computer Science, AS transfer degree with a 60-credit minimum; the enumerated requirements model a 60-61 credit range.
Both degree trees close honestly at the 60-credit minimum, while source contradictions and unsupported cross-choice rules remain explicit analysis blockers.

institutions.name: Blue Ridge Community College

catalog.evidence: The current catalog header identifies the 2026-2027 Catalog and Student Handbook; the program overview prints Award: Associate of Science Degree and Major: Computer Science.

degree.purpose: Transfer preparation for a baccalaureate program in computer science or a related field.
degree.official_requirement_structure: The four-semester Plan of Study Grid is the only official course-requirement table. It is reorganized by requirement in composition; the semester ordering is not imported as an extra schedule rule.

general_education_elective.rule: choose from the official program-owned General Education Electives table
general_education_elective.conflict: The official menu includes three-credit CST 100, CST 110, MTH 245, ASL 201, SPA 201, and SPA 202, but the program grid assigns four credits to the slot and states no compensating-credit rule.

computer_science_electives.rule: Complete nine credits from the program-owned Computer Science Electives table; no universal course count is printed.
computer_science_electives.duplicate_credit_rule: Students may not receive graduation credit for both MTH 167 and MTH 161, or both MTH 167 and MTH 162.

ucgs_block_ii_humanities_art_literature.rule: choose two three-credit courses from different categories

credit_arithmetic.closure: The printed slot values close exactly at 60-62. A student selecting a three-credit course in the printed four-credit General Education Elective slot does not close without an unstated adjustment, so that route remains blocked for deterministic analysis.

important_constraints: The two Block II courses must come from different Art, Humanities, or Literature categories.
No credit may be awarded for both ECO 150 and ECO 201 or ECO 202.
No credit may be awarded for both MTH 155 and MTH 245.
No credit may be awarded for both MTH 167 and MTH 161 or MTH 162.

residency.unit: percent of degree credits completed at Blue Ridge

other_rules: Complete all curriculum requirements and receive the required recommendation and certification.
Resolve financial obligations and complete the graduation application.
Participate in general-education assessment when selected.

source_conflicts_and_analysis_blockers: A four-credit General Education Elective slot offers multiple three-credit courses with no published compensating-credit instruction.
The two Block II choices require distinct categories, a cross-choice rule not implemented by the evaluator.
The nine-credit Computer Science elective menu includes two-, three-, four-, and five-credit courses but states no choose-N rule.
Several elective menus overlap fixed or other choice menus, so applied-credit double counting must be prevented rather than assumed away.
capture_and_parser_notes: The official CourseLeaf page puts the plan grid in #requiredcoursestextcontainer and all three program-owned elective tables in sibling #computerscienceelectivestextcontainer. Both are children of #content.

A selector that takes only the first match from '#requiredcoursestextcontainer, #computerscienceelectivestextcontainer' would silently lose the elective tables; use #content as the authoritative scope.
The parser may reorganize the grid by rule only in the reviewed composition. It must not import semester placement as a second requirement layer.

sources.evidence: Award identity, official grid, total, lab menu, General Education Elective menu, Computer Science elective menu, and Block II footnote.
Current UCGS Block II, III, and VI course dictionaries and duplicate-credit restrictions.
The eight concrete world-language courses linked by both program-owned elective tables.
The one-credit SDV 100 or SDV 101 options linked by the program grid.
Current GPA, residency, catalog-age, application, and completion policies.

institutions.name: Brightpoint Community College

catalog.evidence: The catalog heading identifies the 2026-2027 Catalog and Student Handbook, and poid 1464 is titled Computer Science, AS.

degree.purpose: Transfer degree for continued study in computer science.

approved_electives.rule: choose two or three courses totaling at least eight credits
approved_electives.important_code_correction: The official code is ITE 152. The existing line-parser artifact incorrectly normalized it as TE152.

advisory_material_excluded: The BIO 101/BIO 102, CHM 111/CHM 112, or PHY 241/PHY 242 sequence printed after the electives is a recommendation, not an additional AND requirement.
The Spring-only statement is explicitly based on historical trends and current planning and may change; it is not an award requirement.

credit_arithmetic.closure: The enumerated requirements close at the published 60-credit minimum. The approved-elective heading prints 8-9, so the modeled maximum is 61 even though the page states only a total minimum.

general_education_and_elective_sources.authority: The current Computer Science, AS program page itself
general_education_and_elective_sources.evidence: The current official degree page prints closed menus for all four breadth slots, four complete lab-science sequences, and sixteen approved electives.

residency.unit: percent of total semester credits earned through Brightpoint credit instruction

other_rules: Complete all course and credit-hour requirements applicable to the degree.
Credits awarded through experiential learning do not satisfy the residency requirement.
Meet all financial and administrative graduation obligations.

source_conflicts_and_analysis_blockers: The approved-elective rule combines a variable choose-two-or-three cardinality with an eight-credit minimum; a simple choose-two evaluator is insufficient for two three-credit selections.
Approved electives overlap laboratory-science courses. The same applied credits cannot silently satisfy both the eight-credit sequence and the separate eight-credit elective slot.
The catalog prints a 60-credit minimum but no overall maximum; the enumerated 8-9 elective range produces a modeled 60-61 range.
capture_and_parser_notes: The repository's former catoid 8, poid 1008 seed is stale. Current identity is catoid 12, poid 1464, returnto 1157.
The current host can return an AWS WAF 202 response with an empty body to direct HTTP clients; browser-capable Acalog capture reaches the official page.

The line parser currently drops the leading I from ITE 152 and can ingest the advisory science recommendation into the final Approved Electives group. Composition corrects both without editing the raw artifact.

sources.evidence: Award identity, fixed courses, lab sequences, approved breadth/elective menus, and published minimum.
Current completion, 25-percent residency, GPA, and experiential-learning rules.
Current academic-standing and curriculum-completion policy context.
